one_month_reasoning: The main scheduled event in the window is Q3 2026 earnings on 2026-10-29, before the open (10:00 ET call) [15], two trading days before 2026-10-31. Consensus Q3 is about $9.8-9.9 EPS on $22.1-22.4B revenue [19]. FY26 consensus ($88.46B / $36.93) sits above the $85-87B / $35.50-36.50 guide [19][2], and Q2 beat by about $2 ($8.38 vs ~$6.07-6.58) despite $3.03 of IPR&D [18], so a revenue beat-and-raise is the more likely outcome and is largely priced in. Skeptic offsets inside the print: (a) Q3 non-GAAP EPS will absorb acquired IPR&D from deals that closed after June 30 (AtaiBeckley, $2.8B upfront [44][45], plus the three vaccine developers, up to $3.8B [31]); Lilly's guide excludes post-June IPR&D [49], so the EPS headline and the FY EPS guide may be mechanically lowered even if revenue is raised. The market looked through this in Q2, so I treat it as headline noise, not a fundamental miss. (b) First full quarter of the Medicare Bridge at about $245 net: 700k seniors with 70% on Lilly [47] lifts volume but dilutes average net price. The 7th Circuit retatrutide classification opinion (argued 2026-09-24 [39][40]) could land in the window, but rulings typically take months; it matters for the long-term multiple, not for near-term EPS. The CagriSema decision most likely falls around mid-December, outside the window. Correction from round 1: September was flat ($1,156.73 on Aug 31 to $1,157.08 on Sep 30 [48]), so there is no September sell-off to mean-revert and I drop that tilt. Lognormal with median $1,152 (essentially spot, a hair of drift for the beat-and-raise pattern) and a one-month sigma of 10.5%, slightly above 35%/3.5 for the print.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods. (1) Horizon NTM EPS $49.63 (25% of 2027 EPS $46.25 plus 75% of 2028 EPS $50.75, both = consensus less a $1.25/share recurring IPR&D allowance) x 24x = $1,191, weight 0.5. (2) Consensus 2027 EPS $47.51 x 23x = $1,093, weight 0.3. (3) Morningstar's $980 DCF rolled forward 12 months = about $1,040, weight 0.2. Blended: about $1,130, about 2% below today's price.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Horizon (Oct-2027) NTM EPS $49.63 x 24x forward P/E; EPS = consensus less an explicit $1.25/share expected acquired-IPR&D allowance

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus 2027 EPS $47.51 (30 analysts, range $40.73-54.94; revisions 19 up / 4 down) [19][20] less $1.25/share of expected acquired IPR&D. Lilly's non-GAAP EPS absorbs IPR&D and its guidance excludes unannounced deals [49]; 2026 absorbed $3.03 in Q2 alone [18] and Q3 will add AtaiBeckley ($2.8B upfront [44]) and the vaccine deals (up to $3.8B [31]), so a $1.25 allowance (~$1.1B after tax) for 2027 is conservative. Per the supervisor, I no longer also haircut for price: the Jan-2027 price reset is carried in the bear scenario and left-tail component instead.

Published 2028 consensus is $51.01 (MarketScreener, on revenue +11.6% to $113.9B) [41] to $52.69 (ChartMill) [42]; I take ~$52.0 and deduct the same $1.25 IPR&D allowance. This replaces my round-1 $52.50, which compounded my 2027 figure at the 2027 revenue growth rate (+15.4%) and so sat above consensus once the haircut is netted.

Today's NTM P/E is about 25.6x on consensus [19]; 5-year mean 34.6x, industry 18.0x [4]; Franke's skeptic benchmark 23.7x 2027 [5]; Morningstar's DCF implies ~27x 2026 [21]. EPS growth halves from ~29% (2027) to ~10% (2028), the Medicare Bridge ends 2027-12-31 with no successor [37], and the retatrutide BLA/NDA ruling is pending [39]: all argue for modest de-rating to 24x by Oct 2027.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Consensus 2027 EPS $47.51 x 23x (de-rated, near the skeptic benchmark)

inputs_detail.derivation: Franke's skeptic benchmark is 23.7x 2027 [5]. HSBC (Reduce, PT $940 since 10 Sep 2026 [16], $850 at the March downgrade [17]) implies about 20x. I use 23x: bear-tilted, but not HSBC's TAM-correction case. Unchanged from round 1; this leg uses unadjusted consensus as a check on my IPR&D haircut.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Morningstar DCF fair value $980 (6 Aug 2026), rolled forward 12 months at about 8% cost of equity less a 0.6% dividend yield

inputs_detail.derivation: Morningstar raised it from $900 to $980 after Q2 on higher long-term margins plus a pipeline placeholder. It implies about 27x 2026 EPS. I use it as an independent cash-flow cross-check, since my own FCF base is distorted by capex.
About 8% cost of equity minus about 1.7% paid out as dividends and buybacks (H1-26 dividends $3.09B plus buybacks $3.96B on about $1.03T [12]) gives about 6%. 980 x 1.06 = $1,039.

inputs_detail.value: H1-26 FCF $10.8B (OCF $16.0B less capex $5.26B); about 2.1% FCF yield annualised
inputs_detail.derivation: This supports a cash-flow value below the P/E methods while capex runs near a third of OCF. Net debt is about $46B ($7.05B + $47.86B debt less $8.95B cash), about $51/share.

bear.story: The Jan-2027 US price reset (Novo $675 list price [8], CVS co-preferred, Medicare $245 [9]) outruns volume; the Foundayo uptick stalls well short of Guggenheim's $1.8B [46]; ex-US generic semaglutide spreads [10][36]. 2027 EPS is cut toward $41-42 [19] with 2028 near flat, and the multiple compresses to ~19-20x as the Bridge's end-2027 expiry with no successor [37] and an adverse 7th Circuit ruling (NDA, 5-year exclusivity for retatrutide) [39][40] weigh on terminal value. A retatrutide label problem [27] or another large IPR&D-heavy deal [44] adds to it.

base.story: Volume outruns price, as in Q2 (US volume +37%, price -3%) [18], helped by 700k Bridge starts with 70% on Lilly [47] and Foundayo at about a third of new oral starts [46]. EPS tracks consensus less recurring IPR&D (2027 ~$46.25, 2028 ~$50.75); retatrutide is filed in Q1 2027; the NTM multiple drifts from ~25.6x to ~24x: roughly +3.5%.

bull.story: The Bridge drives a prescription inflection and a permanent coverage path emerges; Foundayo beats Guggenheim's raised forecasts [46]; 2027 EPS tracks the top of the range ($50+) [19]; the 7th Circuit orders BLA treatment (12-year exclusivity) [39]. Re-rating toward the Citi $1,600 / Berenberg $1,400 targets [38][34]: about $55 NTM EPS x 28x.

thesis_break_reason: About 24% below today, below the lowest Street target ($930 [20]) and about 18.3x 2027 consensus EPS [19]. Getting there in a non-crashing market would need the 2027 consensus cut toward $40-42: evidence that US net price declines after the Jan-2027 reset are outrunning volume, a genuine safety/label problem for tirzepatide, Foundayo or retatrutide, or an adverse retatrutide classification ruling combined with estimate cuts. The September path ($1,280 on Aug 19 to $1,115.70 on Sep 11, -13%, with no estimate cuts [48]) shows a drawdown to the low $1,100s is ordinary volatility, so the break must sit well below that. I keep $870 rather than the supervisor's $840: as the skeptic, I would rather flag the break before the stock reaches a pharma-like ~17.7x, at which point the damage is done. Credit (Aa3/AA-, positive outlooks [11]), the tariff exemption through Jan-2029 [28][29] and short interest of 0.84% of float [30] mean no balance-sheet or forced-flow path gets there on its own.

reasoning: Round 2. I re-read the supervisor's file and ran 8 follow-up searches plus one price-data pull. The supervisor graded my sources high and in lane; I act on its three points for me. (1) IPR&D-only haircut: my round-1 2027 haircut mixed price and IPR&D. I now take consensus EPS and deduct only an explicit $1.25/share recurring IPR&D allowance. New evidence backs it: Q3 will absorb AtaiBeckley ($2.8B upfront, closed in September [44][45]) and the three vaccine deals [31], none of them in the guide [49]. Price-reset risk now lives only in the bear scenario and the left-tail component, which answers the double-counting question. (2) 2028 consensus: published 2028 EPS is $51.0-52.7 [41][42] on ~11.6% revenue growth. My round-1 2028 figure ($52.50) compounded my 2027 at +15.4%, so net of the haircut it sat above consensus; I re-base to $52.0 less $1.25 = $50.75. That lowers the main P/E leg from $1,218 to $1,191 and fair value from $1,145 to $1,130. I diverge from the supervisor's ~$1,160 because I count recurring IPR&D as a real cost and keep a de-rating to 24x for a 2028 coverage cliff [37] and a pending exclusivity ruling [39][40]. (3) September: I verified the daily closes [48]. It was flat; the Zacks/24/7 'fell' headlines measured from the Aug 19 high, so I drop the mean-reversion tilt from the 1-month view. I also add the 7th Circuit retatrutide classification ruling as a dated skeptic catalyst. Confirmed positives: 700k Bridge starts, 70% on Lilly [47]; Foundayo at 47.5k weekly scripts with Guggenheim at $1.8B in 2027 [46]. The bear case is still price and multiple, not solvency or fraud: Aa3/AA- positive [11], net debt ~$46B [12], short interest 0.84% [30], small insider sales [16], no short-seller report found. Scenarios: bear $830 (0.23), base $1,190 (0.53), bull $1,540 (0.24); mean ~$1,191. Ladder: a mixture of 85% lognormal (median $1,180, sigma 29%) and 15% left-tail lognormal (median $980, sigma 40%). The tail weight is cut from 20% to 15% because the price reset is no longer also in base EPS. That gives a median of ~$1,155, P(>= spot) 0.507, and a right tail slightly thinner than round 1, in line with ~10% 2028 growth. Limits: Morningstar, Bloomberg and ChartMill were reached only via search snippets; the Q3 IPR&D amount is my estimate pending Lilly's 8-K.
